turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `composition` (absorber), `architecture` (n-i-p =
regular, p-i-n = inverted), `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode),
`etl` (electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Each row is a device
CONFIGURATION whose efficiency is the median over at least 2 independently
fabricated cells, so it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single
champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_retention_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured
    percentage of the initial efficiency still retained at the end of a
    300–1200 h stability test (%).
  - b3_pvk_retention_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose percentage
    of the initial efficiency still retained at the end of a 300–1200 h
    stability test (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and the same
    device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST percentage
of the initial efficiency still retained at the end of a 300–1200 h
stability test (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
The highest-retention devices in the training set share a small number of physically motivated features: an all-inorganic or Cs-rich absorber (intrinsically higher thermal/moisture/phase stability than MA-rich compositions), an inert carbon electrode or a dopant-free/inorganic hole selector (eliminating hygroscopic LiTFSI and metal-halide reactions), a chemically robust electron selector (SnO2 or a thin fullerene/BCP stack rather than photocatalytic TiO2 or hydroxyl-rich ZnO), and contact buffers that suppress ion and metal diffusion.  

c074 realises essentially all of these advantages (CsPbBr, mesoporous TiO2 plus graphene-QDs, HTL-free carbon). Analogous carbon-CsPbBr cells retain 95–99 %.  
c052 replaces the absorber with a still-robust CsFAMA composition while keeping the carbon electrode and adding the hydrophobic, dopant-free CuPc selector; the closest training analogue retains 94 %.  
c076 uses the UV-stable SnO2 ETL together with an SWCNT interlayer that both extracts holes and acts as a moisture/ion barrier around Spiro; related CNT- or oxide-buffered CsFAMA cells retain ~92–93 %.  
c069 is an inverted stack whose PTAA (typically undoped) and Cu electrode avoid AgI formation and Li-salt ingress, while C60/BCP provides excellent electron selectivity and ion blocking; the nearest CsFAMA analogue retains 91.5 %.  
c062 is an all-inorganic CsPbBrI cell whose compact-TiO2/Spiro/Au stack is almost identical to a training device that already retains 91 %; the slightly more noble Au contact is expected to be at least as good.  

These five candidates therefore sit at the top of the stability ranking implied by both the training distribution and device-physics considerations.

Final: c074, c052, c076, c069, c062
